title: Proteomic analysis of aqueous humor from patients with Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy reveals downregulated expression of HSP60
task: Identify proteomic biomarkers in aqueous humor of Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy patients
key_results: 48 proteins significantly downregulated in FECD vs controls; HSP60 reduced in both AqH and corneal endothelial tissue from FECD patients
comments: HSP60 involvement suggests mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis may underlie FECD pathology, but functional validation is needed to establish causality.

inputs: aqueous humor samples from FECD mild patients
aqueous humor samples from FECD advanced patients
aqueous humor samples from control subjects

hypotheses.hypothesis: HSP60 downregulation is associated with FECD pathology
hypotheses.result: Confirmed through reduced expression in both AqH and corneal endothelial tissue samples

hypotheses.hypothesis: DEPs are involved in energy metabolism and cytoskeletal function
hypotheses.result: Functional enrichment analysis supported this hypothesis

title: Deep learning technique for rice leaf disease classification and severity level identification via Hybrid ResConvolutional Neural Network
task: Rice leaf disease classification and severity identification from images
key_results: HyResCN-Net achieved 94.258% accuracy, 96.479% TPR, 92.898% TNR, 91.312% precision, and 93.824% F1-score on Rice Leaf Bacterial and Fungal Disease Dataset
comments: Strong performance on a specialized agricultural dataset, but comparison to simpler baselines and ablation studies are missing to assess the contribution of individual components.

model_io.model: HyResCN-Net (Hybrid ResConvolutional Neural Network integrating PCNN and ResNeXt)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Integration of PCNN and ResNeXt improves discriminative learning for disease classification
hypotheses.result: HyResCN-Net achieved competitive accuracy metrics on Rice Leaf Dataset

hypotheses.hypothesis: Feature extraction (entropy, GDP, CLBP, histograms) enhances disease representation
hypotheses.result: Not explicitly validated via ablation; contribution unclear

title: Machine learning identifies plasma-derived exosomal miRNAs associated with low muscle mass in Tibetan patients with rheumatoid arthritis
task: Identification of plasma-derived exosomal miRNAs associated with low muscle mass in rheumatoid arthritis patients
key_results: Machine learning identified hsa-miR-1294 and hsa-let-7c-5p as candidate miRNA features; miRNA-based and target gene-based nomogram models showed AUC of 0.905 in development datasets; integrated network analysis retained 50 candidate target genes and 43 miRNAs
comments: Exploratory study with limited statistical power after multiple-testing correction; candidate compounds identified but validation is needed before clinical application.

inputs: miRNA features or target gene features

hypotheses.hypothesis: Plasma exosomal miRNAs are biomarkers for low muscle mass in RA patients
hypotheses.result: hsa-miR-1294 and hsa-let-7c-5p identified as candidate features; nomogram AUC 0.905 in development data

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dysregulated miRNAs modulate sphingolipid metabolism and oxidative phosphorylation
hypotheses.result: Functional enrichment identified these metabolic pathways as nominally enriched

title: ConvSNN: an energy-efficient hybrid convolutional-spiking neural network for wrist-worn stress and affective state recognition
task: Energy-efficient stress and affective state recognition from wrist-worn physiological signals
key_results: ConvSNN achieved 98.07% accuracy on random split and 94.0% under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on WESAD; estimated per-inference energy of 48.31 μJ at 5.70 ms latency; temperature scaling reduced calibration error from 0.149 to 0.017
comments: Excellent subject-generalization results, but energy estimates are emulated rather than measured on actual embedded hardware, limiting claims of real-world deployment feasibility.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hybrid convolutional-spiking architecture balances accuracy and energy efficiency
hypotheses.result: Achieved 94% LOSO accuracy with 48.31 μJ per-inference energy

hypotheses.hypothesis: Time-to-first-spike classification head with spiking confidence gate improves robustness
hypotheses.result: 5.9 percentage-point accuracy gap between accepted and rejected windows supports principled abstention

hypotheses.hypothesis: Temperature scaling improves probability calibration without sacrificing accuracy
hypotheses.result: Expected calibration error reduced from 0.149 to 0.017 with no accuracy change

title: Evaluating parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models for sentiment analysis with bayesian optimization
task: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models for Arabic sentiment analysis
key_results: SILMA-9B-Instruct achieved F1-scores of 88.95% (ASTD), 89.91% (LABR), and 96.55% (HARD); LoRA with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization reduced computational cost while maintaining competitive performance
comments: Bayesian optimization framework is well-motivated for LoRA hyperparameter tuning, but the paper lacks detailed comparison of computational savings versus standard fine-tuning.

hypotheses.hypothesis: LoRA fine-tuning achieves competitive performance with reduced parameters compared to full fine-tuning
hypotheses.result: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and SILMA-9B-Instruct showed competitive F1-scores

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bayesian optimization finds superior LoRA configurations versus grid/random search
hypotheses.result: Not explicitly compared; optimization results shown but no baseline comparison

title: Comparative evaluation of statistical learning methods for polygenic prediction in UK Biobank
task: Comparative evaluation of polygenic risk score methods across different genetic architectures
key_results: Non-infinitesimal models (LDpred2, PRS-CS, SBayesR) outperformed infinitesimal models when causal SNP proportion is low; functional annotation-based models (SBayesRC, PolyPred) achieved highest predictive accuracy on UK Biobank traits (height, BMI, type 2 diabetes, glaucoma)
comments: Comprehensive evaluation with both simulations and real data, but results are trait-specific and genetic architecture-dependent, limiting universal applicability.

model_io.model: LDpred2, PRS-CS, SBayesR, SBayesRC, PolyPred, MegaPRS

hypotheses.hypothesis: Non-infinitesimal models outperform infinitesimal models under sparse causal architecture
hypotheses.result: Confirmed in simulations and UK Biobank validation cohorts

hypotheses.hypothesis: Functional genomic annotations improve prediction accuracy
hypotheses.result: SBayesRC and PolyPred (annotation-based) achieved highest real-data accuracy

hypotheses.hypothesis: Optimal PRS method depends on underlying genetic architecture and trait characteristics
hypotheses.result: Performance varied by trait; no single method optimal across all phenotypes

title: A secure multilayer audio encryption scheme based on chain ring algebraic S-boxes, Rössler diffusion, and 4D hyperchaotic permutation
task: Secure audio encryption using chain-ring S-boxes, Rössler diffusion, and 4D hyperchaotic permutation
key_results: S-boxes achieve nonlinearity 112 with differential approximation probability 0.0148; encrypted audio entropy 15.8999 bits; NPCR 99.6783%, UACI 33.4%; full NIST SP 800-22 passage; 28-second audio encrypted in 0.2855s
comments: Cryptanalytic evaluation is thorough but use of commutative chain ring for S-box design lacks established security bounds compared to well-studied algebraic structures.

model_io.model: Three-stage audio encryption: Rössler diffusion → 4D Lü hyperchaotic permutation → dual S-box substitution

hypotheses.hypothesis: Chain ring R₁₃ = F₂[x]/⟨x¹³⟩ enables high-nonlinearity S-boxes comparable to or exceeding GF(2⁸)-based designs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: nonlinearity 112, differential probability 0.0148

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dual independent chaotic systems for diffusion and permutation provide stronger confusion-diffusion than single system
hypotheses.result: Supported: entropy 15.8999 bits, NPCR 99.6783%, UACI 33.4%, full NIST passage

title: Vehicle CO₂ emission prediction based on firefly with ant colony optimization tuned long short-term memory model
task: Vehicle CO₂ emission prediction via FA-ACO-LSTM with feature selection and hyperparameter tuning
key_results: FA-ACO-LSTM achieves MSE 0.0099, MAE 0.0791, R² 98.71%; 45% MSE reduction vs. untuned LSTM (R² improved 96.53%→98.71%); BFA feature selection outperforms BMWO/BFO/BGWO
comments: Strong performance but dataset is cross-sectional not temporal, making LSTM interpretation as feature-interaction learner rather than forecaster; fuel-consumption proxies account for substantial predictive value, limiting model's utility for pure vehicle-attribute prediction.

model_io.model: FA-ACO hyperparameter tuning scheduler selecting among LSTM, CNN, GRU, MLP, TabNet
inputs: vehicle descriptors (22,556 vehicles from Canadian registry); feature selection via Binary Firefly Algorithm

hypotheses.hypothesis: FA-ACO joint tuning of rank, inertia, and learning rate for LSTM outperforms single-algorithm or grid-search baselines
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: FA-ACO-LSTM R²=98.71% vs. FA-ACO-CNN (93.55%), GRU (90.03%), MLP (87.60%), TabNet (84.88%); ANOVA F=30.2, p<0.0001

hypotheses.hypothesis: Binary Firefly feature selection minimizes error and identifies fuel-consumption proxies as dominant predictors
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: fuel-consumption features critical (R² drops from 98.71% to 88.08% when excluded); BFA lowest average error vs. other wrappers

title: Bifurcation analysis of continuous and discrete time predator-prey models with habitat complexity
task: Bifurcation analysis of continuous and discrete predator-prey models with habitat complexity
key_results: Hopf, transcritical, and Neimark-Sacker bifurcations characterized; Turing instability analyzed for reaction-diffusion system; theoretical results validated by numerical simulation
comments: Study focuses on linear stability analysis but lacks global bifurcation diagram or chaos detection; biological interpretation of habitat complexity parameter could be strengthened.

model_io.model: Continuous-time predator-prey system with Holling Type II response
Forward Euler discretization of predator-prey model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Habitat complexity induces Hopf and transcritical bifurcations in continuous model
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: bifurcation analysis establishes parameter regimes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discrete analog exhibits Neimark-Sacker bifurcation distinct from continuous case
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: discretization introduces bifurcation phenomena

title: CFD-based recurrent neural network modeling of plasma-assisted flow control over a stepped NACA4412 airfoil using LSTM and GRU
task: Aerodynamic flow field prediction over stepped airfoil with plasma actuation
key_results: LSTM/GRU models accurately predict velocity contours; combined BFS+plasma configuration achieved 83.07% lift improvement and 44.43% L/D enhancement
comments: Hybrid CFD-ML approach demonstrates surrogate modeling capability but is restricted to single Reynolds number (3.1×10⁶) and limited angle-of-attack range.

inputs: time-resolved velocity field data from SST k-ω CFD simulations (Re=3.1×10⁶, AOA 0°–20°)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dual AC-DBD plasma actuators improve flow control by delaying separation and weakening vortical structures
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: maximum lift improvement 83.07% for 30%c BFS case; peak L/D enhancement 44.43% for 10%c BFS case

hypotheses.hypothesis: RNN surrogates can efficiently capture unsteady aerodynamic responses
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: trained models accurately predicted velocity contours with strong agreement to CFD

title: Two scale black holes with a phenomenological suppression profile: extremality, null critical curves, and test field spectra
task: Characterization of two-scale black hole metrics with phenomenological suppression
key_results: Derived exact extremal boundary with two parametric branches; Ricci and Kretschmann scalars vanish at center; test-field WKB accuracy 0.22% and time-domain 0.48% relative to pseudospectral reference
comments: Theoretical analysis is rigorous but physically motivated suppression profile remains phenomenological; connection to quantum gravity or observational constraints unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Phenomenological short-distance suppression factor maintains regularity at center while modifying effective mass
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Ricci and Kretschmann scalars vanish; orthonormal curvature components remain bounded; metric admits local C⁴ Cartesian extension

hypotheses.hypothesis: WKB approximation and time-domain evolution agree with pseudospectral computation for scalar and EM test fields
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: largest relative differences 0.22% (WKB) and 0.48% (time evolution)

title: Novel adaptive fixed-time synchronization for fractional-order uncertain Hopfield neural networks with proportional delays of unbounded nature
task: Fixed-time synchronization of fractional-order Hopfield neural networks with unbounded proportional delays
key_results: Novel adaptive controller achieves fixed-time synchronization; settling time governed by control parameters and can be effectively estimated; criteria obtained via Lyapunov function method
comments: Proportional delays are physically motivated but theoretical conditions are complex; experimental validation on actual neural systems is absent.

model_io.model: Adaptive control law with three functional modules
inputs: fractional-order master-slave Hopfield neural network state

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-module adaptive controller (negative feedback + delay suppression + convergence enhancement) enables fixed-time synchronization under unbounded delays
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: new synchronization criteria derived and settling time can be estimated

hypotheses.hypothesis: Control parameters directly govern settling time in fixed-time framework
hypotheses.result: Supported: numerical experiments investigate influence of control parameters

title: A hybrid memetic algorithm for an energy-aware distributed blocking hybrid flowshop scheduling problem with transportation time
task: Distributed blocking hybrid flowshop scheduling with energy and transportation time
key_results: Hybrid memetic algorithm (HMA) achieves competitive solution quality on 100 benchmark instances; multi-objective optimization minimizes makespan and total energy consumption
comments: Paper lacks detailed runtime comparisons and convergence rate analysis versus baseline metaheuristics on large-scale instances.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Three-layer encoding with dual initialization strategies improves population diversity and search efficiency
hypotheses.result: Supported: HMA achieves competitive solution quality across varying problem sizes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Energy-saving neighborhood strategy reduces redundant energy consumption
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: adaptive local search operators strengthen solution refinement

title: A drift adaptive framework for detecting and tracking evolving anomalies in financial transaction streams
task: Drift-adaptive anomaly detection and tracking of evolving fraud populations in financial transaction streams
key_results: HADA+ achieves ROC-AUC 0.915219±0.000954, F1@100 0.068992±0.000337 on Credit Card Fraud; macro-F1 0.9673 on lifecycle validation vs. 0.3674 for baseline; ECS 0.755973±0.000886
comments: Framework is comprehensive and lifecycle-aware but PR-AUC and Precision@100 remain low, suggesting severe class imbalance; computational scalability to large transaction volumes not thoroughly evaluated.

model_io.model: HADA+: Adaptive Anomaly Prioritization (AAP) + Score-Aware Clustering (SAC) + Optimal Transport Lifecycle Alignment (OTLA) + Lifecycle Evolution Modeling (LEM)
inputs: transaction stream (Credit Card Fraud, Mobile Banking, Synthetic Financial, Controlled Lifecycle Validation datasets)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Drift-responsive prioritization and score-aware clustering preserve structural and temporal continuity of anomaly populations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: ECS 0.755973±0.000886 demonstrates stable continuity; five-event macro-F1 0.9673 on lifecycle validation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Optimal Transport Lifecycle Alignment enables accurate cross-window anomaly tracking under concept drift
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 4.1pp performance advantage over nearest-centroid matching; macro-F1 0.9673 vs. 0.3674

title: A multi-task deep learning network for robust and high accuracy star sensor image centroiding
task: Star sensor centroid estimation with binary-star detection
key_results: 100.0% binary-star detection rate; centroid error ≈0.017 pixels (vs. conventional ≈0.16 pixels)
comments: Lightweight multi-task CNN achieves excellent performance but validation is limited to synthetic/simulated datasets without deployment on actual flight hardware.

inputs: star sensor image patches (varying morphologies: Gaussian, non-Gaussian, binary-star)
outputs: binary classification label (single vs. binary star)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Differentiable Gaussian convolution and coordinate attention modules improve robustness to non-Gaussian distortions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: centroid error under non-Gaussian conditions reduced from ≈0.12 pixels (Gaussian fitting) to ≈0.017 pixels

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pareto-optimal loss function enables multi-task learning without manual tuning
hypotheses.result: Supported: single forward pass achieves simultaneous classification and regression

title: Infrared quantum emission and its tuning from boron-nitride nanotube fluors
task: Engineering tunable infrared quantum emission from defect-engineered boron nitride nanotubes
key_results: DFT predicts CB defect zero-phonon-line emission tunable 1000–2000 nm via diameter variation (0.8–0.4 nm); strain tunability 2000–2300 nm; electric field tunability 2000–3400 nm for (5,0) BNNT
comments: Purely computational DFT prediction without experimental validation; excited-state calculations acknowledged as incomplete, limiting reliability for quantum efficiency estimates.

model_io.model: Single-walled BNNT with intrinsic point defects

hypotheses.hypothesis: CB defect centers exhibit tunable near-infrared emission spanning 1000–2000 nm by diameter variation
hypotheses.result: DFT calculations predict ZPL-like emission from (10,0) to (5,0) BNNT structures

hypotheses.hypothesis: Uniaxial strain and electric fields modulate defect electronic structure to enable further emission tuning
hypotheses.result: Strain shifts emission 2000–2300 nm; electric field extends range to 2000–3400 nm for (5,0) BNNT

title: A single passive terahertz metasurface implementing eight Boolean logic gates through polarization multiplexing
task: Passive terahertz metasurface implementing eight Boolean logic gates via polarization multiplexing
key_results: Single 1 THz metasurface realizes OR, AND, XOR, BUFFER and complements NOR, NAND, XNOR, NOT with mean detector contrast 13.22 dB over 16λ₀×16λ₀ aperture; all 28 gate-input combinations validated by full-wave simulation
comments: Clever polarization-encoding strategy increases gate density but measurement relies on spatial masking and intensity thresholding, limiting scalability to practical multi-bit computing architectures.

model_io.model: Passive transmissive THz metasurface with polarization encoding
inputs: 45° linearly polarized THz beam at 1 THz
outputs: output power in designated detector windows

hypotheses.hypothesis: Orthogonal polarization channels enable simultaneous evaluation of complementary logic gates
hypotheses.result: x- and y-polarized phase profiles carry gate and complement; 45° illumination evaluates both via single unit cell

hypotheses.hypothesis: Wavefront encoding via diffractive design correctly routes all gate-input combinations
hypotheses.result: Full-wave FDTD confirms correct logic output for all 28 combinations with minimum contrast 5.88 dB

title: Hybrid plasmonic–photonic multi-Fano resonance refractive index sensor using periodic gold nano-bar assisted microcavity coupling
task: Multi-Fano resonance refractive index sensor design via plasmonic-photonic coupling
key_results: Sensitivity of 975 nm/RIU and figure of merit of 139.28 at Mode 5 through geometric optimization of gold nano-bar-microcavity structure
comments: Numerical study lacking experimental validation; practical fabrication tolerances and temperature stability not addressed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-Fano resonances arise from hybrid plasmon-cavity mode coupling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via electric field distribution analysis showing localized field enhancements at resonance modes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Linear dependence of resonance wavelength on surrounding refractive index enables sensing
hypotheses.result: Demonstrated with highest sensitivity of 975 nm/RIU extracted from spectral fitting slopes
